prompt:
Create a landscape-format art direction concept board for an isometric train logistics game, headed "CONNECTED HILLS — TILE FAMILY CONCEPT". Use all three attached images strictly as STYLE REFERENCES: first grass texture, second the approved grassy rocky hill silhouette and pixel-cluster illustration, third approved rocky mountain. Preserve their olive moss palette, small visible grass strokes, crisp hand-painted pixel clusters, pale slate stone, fixed orthographic 2:1 isometric view and upper-left light. NO smooth generic noise field, NO clay or glossy low-poly style, NO grassy cube platforms or repeated standalone pyramids.

Layout: on warm neutral background, top half show eight separated, clearly labeled modular landform studies in two rows: "Low slope", "Outer shoulder", "Inner saddle", "Ridge", "Plateau", "Rock face", "High shoulder", "Peak". These are parts of one continuous hillside surface, not eight isolated full mountains. Each must align to same diamond ground footprint and camera. Grassy ramps rise to shared edge heights; ridges join shoulders; only peak has pointed top. Small variations of tufts and exposed rock match references. No large artificial bases under each study.
Bottom half is a large assembled 6 by 6 tile landscape demonstrating contiguous foothill ramps leading into connected stepped elevation bands, broad ridge and two unequal rocky peaks separated by a saddle. Keep tile boundaries invisible in the beauty render, with a small adjacent line diagram indicating levels 0, 1, 2, 3. Peaks arise from shared elevated mass rather than sitting separately on flat ground. Edge-matching landforms should be visually intelligible. A small tree at foot provides scale. Caption "Illustrated surfaces + matching edge heights". This is a visual proposal only, not a screenshot or production-ready tile atlas. Excellent legible layout, no UI chrome.
